extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policy makers, WIPO readers, trademark office staff and researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitional standards used in WIPO's reporting of trademark activity (applications, classes, registrations, origin/residence, sector breakdowns and normalization by GDP/population). Useful for preparing, comparing or interpreting trademark statistics across offices and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an application at a regional IP office is equivalent to filing an application in every member country of the organization that established that particular regional office; the corresponding number of member states multiplies the application. The same multiplier is applied to the classes specified in such an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an application filed at the EUIPO in 2022 by an applicant residing outside the EU is counted as 27 applications abroad (equal to the number of EU member countries); an application filed by an EU resident results in 1 resident application and 26 applications abroad. The concept is employed for reporting data based on an applicant’s origin. Note: equivalent application class counts differ from absolute class counts (which do not take the regional-office multiplier into account).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident (origin) classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed by applicants at their national or regional office are resident applications; applications filed at foreign offices are applications abroad. Office data classifies applications received by an office from both residents and non-residents; origin data presents applications based on the applicant's place of residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark statistics are presented based on an applicant’s place of residence to complement office-level data. When reporting filing abroad by origin, use equivalent application class counts to account for regional office multipliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class count (class counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of Nice classes specified in trademark applications (class counts) used instead of application counts to make filing activity internationally comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class counts enable comparisons across offices despite different single-class vs multi-class filing systems. Note, however, that some figures/data (e.g., trends in ‘numbers of applications filed’) may not adjust for single-class vs multi-class differences — check the figure notes. WIPO totals include Paris-route direct filings and Madrid System designations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Nice Classification (classes and top classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nice Classification of goods and services is used in the international trademark system (and at certain national/regional offices) to categorize trademarks by goods/services class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics report distribution of non-resident filing by Nice classes (e.g., class 9, class 35, class 42, etc.). Top classes and their shares (e.g., top five classes accounting for X% of non-resident filing) are reported to indicate relative importance of goods/services types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping Nice classes into industry sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: The 45 Nice classes are grouped into 10 industry sectors to provide higher-level insights into filing patterns (e.g., research & technology, health, clothing and accessories, leisure & education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sector grouping to report sectoral shares of non-resident filing and compare across offices and origins (figures showing sector shares at top offices and origins are provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization by GDP (resident class count per USD 100 billion GDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident trademark application class counts are adjusted according to GDP to allow comparison of filing intensity relative to economic size (resident application class count per USD 100 billion GDP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both levels and change over time (e.g., 2012 vs 2022) to identify countries with high ratios or significant increases (examples: China, Republic of Korea, Brazil, Russian Federation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization by population (resident class count per million population)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application class counts can be expressed per million population to indicate filing intensity relative to population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this metric to highlight countries with particularly intensive filing per capita (examples: Türkiye, Republic of Korea, China, Switzerland) and to compare across population sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing abroad ratio / share of filing abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Share (percentage) of an origin's total filing that is directed towards protection abroad (applications filed outside the applicant's country), measured using equivalent application class counts or absolute counts depending on context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both absolute counts and shares. Examples: China had 95.1% of class counts destined solely for protection within China in 2022 (4.9% abroad); contrasts shown between economies and income groups. Use this to characterize domestic-orientation vs internationalization of applicants from each origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident share and distribution by origin at offices
rubrics_metrics.description: For each receiving office, the share and distribution of non-resident filing by origin (e.g., percent of non-resident filing in China from US applicants) are reported to show which origins dominate foreign filings at particular offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show shares of non-resident filing by origin for selected offices (e.g., in 2022 almost a quarter of non-resident filing in China came from US applicants). Use to analyze cross-border filing flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend metrics (applications, application class counts, registrations, registration class counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-series measures of total applications, application class counts, registrations and registration class counts (e.g., trends from 2008–2022) and their year-on-year growth rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious interpreting registration counts for a given year relative to applications filed in the same year because registrations follow examination and processing lags. Report both counts and growth rates, with notes on major year-to-year changes and contributing offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration class counts and active registrations (registrations in force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of classes specified in issued registrations and counts of active registrations maintained in force via renewals at offices; registrations-in-force indicate the stock of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report estimated global numbers (e.g., 9.3 million registrations recorded in 2022; 12.4 million classes specified) and stocks by office (registrations in force by office). Note reasons for year-to-year fluctuations (application volumes, office examination resources, renewal behavior). Provide distributions by year of initial registration and average age metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability metric: registrations in force by year of initial registration / average age
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of registrations in force according to the year of their initial registration and average age of trademarks in force at selected offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentage of older cohorts still in force (e.g., 22.1% of trademarks registered in 1998 remained in force in 2022) and the share of recent registrations (e.g., for trademarks registered in 2014 or later percentage surpasses 75%). Use to indicate longevity of marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedural data metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural indicators for trademark offices such as distribution of examination outcomes, potentially pending trademark applications, number of trademark examiners, duration of trademark examination, third-party oppositions, and appeals against decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics (listed as B38–B43) are used to assess office performance and procedural backlog; present them alongside application/registration counts to contextualize registration/processing volumes and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and source notes (WIPO estimates and included routes)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO totals and figures are WIPO estimates based on data covering a specified number of IP offices (e.g., 168 offices) and include direct filings (Paris route) and Madrid System designations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report the scope and data sources (offices covered, routes included) and note caveats such as differences across offices in single-class vs multi-class systems and the multiplier effect of regional offices like EUIPO when interpreting cross-country comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability caveats (single-class vs multi-class, regional multipliers, timing differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit warnings that differences in national/regional filing systems (single-class vs multi-class), the multiplier effect of regional offices, and timing differences between filing and registration can affect comparability of raw counts across offices and over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing offices or years, adjust or interpret data accordingly (use class counts, equivalent class counts, normalize by GDP/population, and note examination/registration lags). Figures and table notes often call out these comparability issues.
